title: An Information-Flow Perspective on Explainability Requirements: Specification and Verification
abstract: arXiv:2509.01479v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Explainable systems expose information about why certain observed effects are happening to the agents interacting with them. We argue that this constitutes a positive flow of information that needs to be specified, verified, and balanced against negative information flow that may, e.g., violate privacy guarantees. Since both explainability and privacy require reasoning about knowledge, we tackle these tasks with epistemic temporal logic extended with quantification over counterfactual causes. This allows us to specify that a multi-agent system exposes enough information such that agents acquire knowledge on why some effect occurred. We show how this principle can be used to specify explainability as a system-level requirement and provide an algorithm for checking finite-state models against such specifications. translated_title: 可解释性需求的信息流视角：规范与验证
translated_abstract: 可解释系统向与之交互的智能体暴露关于某些观察到的效应为何发生的信息。我们认为，这构成了一种正向信息流，需要对其进行规范、验证，并与可能违反隐私保证的负向信息流进行平衡。由于可解释性和隐私性都需要对知识进行推理，我们使用扩展了反事实原因量化的认知时序逻辑来处理这些任务。这使我们能够指定一个多智能体系统暴露足够的信息，使智能体获得关于某些效应为何发生的知识。我们展示了如何使用这一原则将可解释性指定为系统级需求，并提供了一种针对此类规范检查有限状态模型的算法。我们展示了该算法的原型实现，并在多个基准上进行了评估，说明了我们的方法的应用。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于信息流的可解释性形式化方法，利用扩展了反事实原因量化的认知时序逻辑，将可解释性指定为系统级需求并提供了验证算法。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an information-flow-based formal approach to explainability, using epistemic temporal logic with counterfactual cause quantification to specify explainability as a system-level requirement and provide a verification algorithm.
